title: Shutter
description: Summer cumulus drifting over the zenith, seen from the foot of five glass towers in Manhattan, looking straight up, on a locked-off frame. Press and hold and the shutter opens on bulb: the frame integrates the light for as long as you hold, so the clouds smear into silk along their wind while the towers, which never moved, stay sharp. An ND filter follows the shutter, so the brightness holds and only time grows. Let go and the long exposure stays on the print until the next press.
intent: After Louis Daguerre's Boulevard du Temple (1838, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boulevard_du_Temple_(photograph)): the street in that plate looks empty because the exposure ran for minutes and the walkers and carriages never stayed in one place long enough to register; only a man having his boots polished stood still and was kept. A photograph keeps what stays. Here the exposure is a real temporal integral of the plate's frames in linear light, offline-baked as a time pyramid of block means so any open interval is a cheap weighted sum, developed through the summer-film pipeline (factory/reality/techniques.md, piece 1).

sources.author: Harshit Joshi (@hpj1992)
sources.note: Hudson Yards, Manhattan, from the foot of five towers looking straight up (Samsung Galaxy S20 FE), published 7 June 2021; 3000x4000 original, turned 90 degrees clockwise (a zenith view has no up) and area-downscaled in linear light to a 1920x1080 band. The photograph is one instant, so the time-lapse is synthesised from it by tools/depth/bakes/shutter/drift.py: the tower mattes from SAM 2.1 Hiera-Tiny (Meta, Apache-2.0) prompts via tools/depth/segment.py, the sky taken apart into its clear-sky gradient and a premultiplied cloud layer (alpha from the loss of the sky's chroma), and a deck of five big cumulus built from the photograph's own (each a few of its clouds scaled 2-3x, laid along the wind and overlapped into one body, one mass dominant, lit from a thickness so the deep crests are a sunlit white and the thin rims and bases a skylight blue, every part slowly breathing) slid behind the towers along one wind in three lanes, periodic over the loop, so the long exposure draws a few broad bands of silk. Looking at the zenith a cloud deck is a plane parallel to the sensor, so its drift is a pure translation. Then the same bake as before: graded in OKLab to a cyan-cobalt that deepens radially toward the zenith, the cloud tops to a cream shoulder and the towers, through their matte, to a warm grey-steel with only their reflected sky a muted cyan (grade.py), integrated along the optical flow, cut into the time pyramid (bake.py), and the clear-sky mean (sky.py); the glass is taken apart per facade into its own light and the photograph's reflection (glass.py), so once the shutter opens each facade mirrors the exposure's own sky across its floor lines and its reflected clouds smear with the real ones. Replaces the first plate, a telephoto crop of the Evolution Tower's crown, Moscow: "Time Lapse Video of Cloud Moving over a Building" by 84LENS (Pexels 5124202, Pexels License, https://www.pexels.com/video/time-lapse-video-of-cloud-moving-over-a-building-5124202/).
